title: Others grant God foreordained each act, but after foreseeing the will's absolutely future determination (Lessius)
source_text: XXI. Ab his autem non multum absunt quidam alii, qui concedunt quidem Deum singulos hominum actus ab aeterno praefiniisse; sed praefinitionem illam sequi praevisionem futurae determinationis ipsius voluntatis. Nec enim ulla hominum opera, etiam quae sunt bona supernaturaliter, in particulari esse praedefinita absoluto decreto Dei, ante praevisam voluntatis nostrae determinationem, non tantum conditionate, sed etiam absolute futuram. Quae est Doctrina Leonardi Lessii Jesuitae in tractatu de Praedestinatione.
pass_a_gloss: XXI. But not far from these are certain others, who indeed concede that God foreordained from eternity the single acts of men; but that that foreordination follows the prevision of the future determination of the will itself. For that no works of men, even those which are supernaturally good, have been in particular predefined by an absolute decree of God, before the foreseen determination of our will, future not only conditionally, but also absolutely. Which is the Doctrine of Leonard Lessius the Jesuit in the treatise on Predestination.
pass_b_english: Not far from these are certain others. They do grant that God foreordained from eternity each single act of men, but say that this foreordination follows his foresight of how the will itself would determine itself.

On their view no human works, not even supernaturally good ones, were predefined in particular by an absolute decree of God before he foresaw our will's determination as future, not only conditionally but also absolutely. This is the teaching of the Jesuit Leonard Lessius in his treatise on predestination.

choices.why: Vasquez's and his sources' verb for God's fixing acts beforehand; 'foreordain' keeps it distinct from praedefinire ('predefine') while showing the near-synonymy.
